problems.title: Local emission normalization does not preserve normalized product-distribution semantics
problems.evidence: Exact single-observation mixture counterexample: correct11/17 versus released-normalization183/296 first-symbol probability.
problems.counterreading: Initializer may remain effective and final trained models may perform well; generic PC product construction still valid with partition corrections.
problems.repair_status: One-observation reweighting verified; full sequential repair unverified

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Read p4 Sections3.1-3.2 product-distribution initialization statement and complete frozen multiply_dense_hmm.py. The program sums log-emissions then row-log-softmaxes them; gamma uses only products of old initial weights, with no statewise emission partition factors.
independent_check.independent_derivation: For the two valid row-stochastic emission matrices in the report and uniform initial weights, freshly enumerated exact Fraction products give Z=(37/50,21/50,8/25,14/25). Product of the observable marginals is(.33,.18), whose normalized first mass is11/17. Averaging locally normalized pair emissions gives(36/37+6/7+1/2+1/7)/4=183/296. Therefore the release operations change the normalized distribution. Reweighting pair priors by Z restores the globally normalized one-observation product.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: This is a one-observation model-semantic diagnostic, not a reconstruction of text8 results or evidence that the heuristic initialization is ineffective. Generic product circuits remain valid when partition corrections propagate. Transition/sequence corrections were not proved.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Minor retained for current-release initialization correspondence; no damage to the core Monarch linear map or trained scalability conclusions demonstrated. Only the one-observation prior reweighting is verified.

problems.title: Color transform printed sign and chroma range are incorrect
problems.evidence: Printed lossy y maps black/white to1/3; code correctly maps to-1/1. Cg=-255 for RGB255,0,255 despite printed0..255.
problems.counterreading: Actual release contains correct minus sign and offsets both chroma channels; historical results not shown corrupt.
problems.repair_status: Local algebra and selected roundtrip calculations verified

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Read original AppendixB.3 p15 and complete static color_trans.py. RGB is normalized to[0,1] for lossy mapping; lossless inputs are integer0..255.
independent_check.independent_derivation: tmp=(r+b)/2,cg=g-tmp, so printed2tmp+cg+1=(r+b)/2+g+1 ranges[1,3]; black=1,white=3 contradict[-1,1]. Correct2tmp+cg-1 agrees with release Y=2*(tmp+Cg/2)-1. Fresh integer arithmetic for(255,0,255) gives(Y,Co,Cg)=(127,0,-255). The stated inverse recovers(0,0,0),(255,255,255),(255,0,255),(0,255,0),(5,12,23) exactly; algebra reconstructs tmp,G,B,R by undoing each integer lifting step.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: Source applies minus1 and offsets both Co and Cg by256; it is direct counterevidence to alleging the printed mistakes were run. Negative chroma has valid larger categorical support. No image-model loss or historical implementation failure is inferred.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Minor retained for reproducibility specification. Correct sign/range and lifting inverse established; no full image loader, quantizer or GPU audit added.
